Lil Durk (whose real name is Durk Banks) was found not guilty on all counts in his federal murder-for-hire trial after his defense team successfully created reasonable doubt regarding his personal involvement in the plot.

Prosecutors had accused the rapper of ordering and funding a targeted hit on rival rapper Quando Rondo in retaliation for the 2020 killing of King Von, an attack that ultimately resulted in the death of Rondo’s cousin, Saviay’a Robinson, near the Beverly Center in Los Angeles in 2022. However, his defense attorneys argued that Durk was not the mastermind behind the scheme and had no direct role in planning or executing the shooting. They pointed the finger at his former personal assistant, Kavon Grant, claiming Grant acted independently without Durk’s knowledge or authorization.

The jury deliberated for three days before reaching a unanimous verdict to acquit him on all five federal charges, which included conspiracy to commit stalking and murder-for-hire. Because federal prosecutors failed to connect Durk directly to the operational orders or prove beyond a reasonable doubt that he financed the retaliatory strike, he was acquitted. However, despite beating the murder-for-hire case, he remained in federal custody to face separate federal racketeering charges.
